Definition: from G1537 and ἐτάζω (to examine); to test thoroughly (by questions), i.e. ascertain or interrogate:--ask, enquire, search.
BiblicalUsage: exetázō is a plain word for ask, enquire, search. In Matthew 2:8, the text says "Go and search diligently for the young child." In Matthew 10:11, the text says "enquire who in it is worthy."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading exetázō this way, I believe discernment is learning to tell the true from the almost-true, by God's Word. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Sends Out the Twelve; The Magi Visit Jesus; Jesus Appears to Seven Disciples by the Sea of Galilee
